cards.text: Joash becomes king of Judah at SEVEN years old, and he reigns in Jerusalem. Friend, I've had oven timers older than that, and not one of them could run a kingdom. His mother is Zibiah, from Beersheba.

cards.question: So the seven-year-old king takes the throne in Jerusalem. How long does Joash reign?

cards.text: Here's the good news, friend. Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, and the text tells us exactly how long that lasts.

cards.question: Joash does what is right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of ___ the priest.
True or false: Jehoiada the priest takes two wives for King Joash.

cards.text: Jehoiada takes two wives for Joash, and Joash has sons and daughters. Then some time later, Joash sets his heart on a big project.

cards.question: What project does King Joash set his heart on?

answers.text: Repairing the house of the LORD

cards.text: So Joash gathers the priests and Levites: go out to the cities of Judah and collect the money due every year from all Israel, to repair the house of your God. Then the king adds, "Do it quickly."

cards.question: True or false: When King Joash tells them to do it quickly, the Levites hurry right out to collect the money.

cards.text: The Levites do NOT make haste, and friend, I know slow: I spent years in a junk drawer watching dust land. So King Joash calls in Jehoiada the high priest with a question.

cards.question: What does King Joash ask Jehoiada the high priest?

answers.text: Why he hasn't made the Levites bring in the tax
Why he hasn't opened the temple doors yet
Why he hasn't offered the morning sacrifice

cards.text: And this isn't some tax Joash made up on the spot. It's the tax Moses the servant of the LORD and the assembly of Israel set for the Tent of the Testimony.

cards.question: Why does the house of God need repairing in the first place?

answers.text: Athaliah's sons broke in and used its sacred objects for the Baals
An earthquake shook the city and cracked its stone walls
Philistine raiders broke in and carried off its doors

cards.text: Athaliah's sons broke in AND used the sacred objects for the Baals, which is NOT what I'd call normal wear and tear. So at King Joash's command, a chest is made.

cards.question: King Joash's chest is placed outside, at the ___ of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then a proclamation goes out across Judah and Jerusalem: bring to the LORD the tax Moses the servant of God set on Israel in the wilderness. Same tax, brand new chest.

cards.question: When the proclamation goes out, how do the officers and the people respond?

answers.text: They rejoice and fill the chest with contributions
They complain but pay what they owe
They wait for the Levites to come collect

cards.text: The people keep dropping their contributions in until that chest is FULL. The Levites bring it to the king's overseers, and when there's a large amount of money, the royal scribe and the high priest's officer empty it and carry it back to its place.

cards.question: How often do the royal scribe and the high priest's officer empty the chest?

cards.text: EVERY SINGLE DAY, friend, and I've seen a cookie jar go from full to empty that fast, but NEVER from empty to full. King Joash and Jehoiada hand the money to the men supervising the work on the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Who do the supervisors hire with the money to restore the house of the LORD?

cards.text: So the workmen labor, and the repair work moves along in their hands.

cards.question: True or false: The workmen rebuild the house of God in a brand new design.

cards.text: They restore the house of God to its specifications, and they reinforce it. And when they finish, there's money LEFT OVER, and friend, I have NEVER in my life seen a repair job come in under budget.

cards.question: What happens to the money left over from repairing the house of the LORD?

answers.text: It's used to make articles for the house of the LORD
It's stored away in the king's treasury
It's handed back to the people of Judah

cards.text: Utensils for the service and the burnt offerings, dishes, and objects of gold and silver. The temple gets a fresh set of everything, and none of it is headed for the back of a drawer.

cards.question: Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings are presented ___ in the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then comes the sad part. Jehoiada the priest grows old and full of years, and he dies.

cards.question: How old is Jehoiada the priest when he dies?

cards.text: ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY, friend, and I felt ancient after a few years in a junk drawer. Now watch where they bury him.

cards.question: Where is Jehoiada the priest buried?

answers.text: With the kings in the City of David
In the cave of Machpelah near Hebron
In a tomb on the Mount of Olives

cards.question: Why is Jehoiada the priest buried with the kings?

answers.text: He did what was good in Israel for God and His temple
He ruled Judah as king while Joash was young
He led Judah's army to a great victory in battle

cards.text: A priest, laid to rest with the kings. And that's where we'll leave Joash for now, friend, because his story is NOT finished.

findings.problem: Stop 2 starts at 2 Chronicles 24:10, but the passage's next stretch starts at 2 Chronicles 24:11.

rule.text: Each stop covers the next stretch of the passage, in order, and gives its verse range.

findings.problem: This true or false card comes straight after card 4 with no story card setting it up. Nothing told so far points to Jehoiada taking wives for Joash, so the baker can only guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The first sentence repeats the answer to card 5 (Jehoiada takes two wives for Joash). Only 'he had sons and daughters' is new from verse 3, so most of the verse 3 part of this card is a recap.

Card 12 is about Moses' tax and gives no setup for why the temple needs repairs. Athaliah has not been mentioned, so the earthquake and Philistine answers are just as likely to a baker who has only seen the earlier cards. This is a pure discovery question on top of cards 2, 4 and 15.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Athaliah's first appearance on a story card never says who she is. She shows up first in card 13's answer, and here she is just 'Athaliah'.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Stop 2's range is 2 Chronicles 24:10-16. That overlaps stop 1 (24:1-10), and verse 10 was already covered in stop 1, so stop 2 does not start at the next stretch.

rule.text: Each stop covers the next stretch of the passage, in order, and gives its verse range.

findings.problem: The first sentence retells verse 10 (the people fill the chest), which stop 1 card 17 already asked and answered, so that part is a recap.
This card has three beats: the people fill the chest, the Levites bring it to the overseers, and the scribe and officer empty it and return it.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'The temple gets a fresh set of everything' is stated as fact, but it goes past verse 14. The verse lists certain articles (utensils, dishes, gold and silver objects). It does not say everything was replaced.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line ('And that's where we'll leave Joash for now, friend, because his story is NOT finished') nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.').

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
